title: tbs_certificate_der's whole purpose has no fixture: a pre-2050 GeneralizedTime
description:
## Why

`tbs_certificate_der` exists for one reason, stated in its own rustdoc:

> x509-cert 0.3 re-encodes the validity times of a `Certificate` under the
> RFC 5280 profile (dates before 2050 become `UTCTime`), so a certificate
> whose issuer used `GeneralizedTime` for such a date would no longer match
> its signature. This function keeps each time in the form it was parsed
> from.

No fixture in the workspace has that shape. Every certificate here encodes
pre-2050 dates as UTCTime, which is what RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5 requires, so
`tbs_certificate_der` and a plain `cert.tbs_certificate().to_der()` return
the same bytes for all of them -- and `tests/public_helpers.rs`, which
verifies four self-signed certificates through it, would pass either way.

The function's purpose is therefore untested. A certificate that trips it
is non-conformant but real: a CA that encoded a 2020 date as
GeneralizedTime produces one, and refusing to verify its signature is a
validation failure for a certificate that is otherwise fine.

## What a fixture needs

A certificate with `notBefore` or `notAfter` before 2050 encoded as
GeneralizedTime, with a valid signature over those bytes.

pyca/cryptography will not emit it -- it follows §4.1.2.5 -- so this is DER
surgery followed by a re-sign, the pattern
`pkix-path/tests/fixtures/dup-ext/gen.py` already uses: rebuild the
TBSCertificate with the time re-tagged, then sign the rebuilt bytes with the
issuer key the generator holds.

The test is then one assertion: the certificate's own key verifies its own
signature over `tbs_certificate_der`'s output, and does not over
`to_der`'s.

## Found by

Writing `tests/public_helpers.rs` (2d0bfec4) for the mutation survivors in
these two helpers, and noticing that the test which kills the mutants does
not reach the rule.
close_reason:
Closed by c9a8b0b0. Three fixtures in pkix-path/tests/fixtures/gentime: both validity times re-tagged as GeneralizedTime, notBefore alone re-tagged, and the conformant original as a control. Built by DER surgery and re-signed; gen.py checks each signature over the bytes it writes out as <name>-tbs.bin, which is the test's oracle.

tests/gentime_validity.rs, four tests. The premise is asserted rather than assumed -- re-encoding through x509-cert's Rfc5280 profile changes the non-conformant fixtures and only those -- so a later x509-cert that stopped normalizing on serialize would report here that tbs_certificate_der has become dead weight. Confirmed the test reaches the purpose: encoding the validity through the profile instead of time-by-time fails three of the four.
